questions.problem:
Given that ${y}_{0}(x)={e}^{x}$ is a particular solution of the Riccati differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{2}-2{e}^{x}y+{e}^{2x}+{e}^{x}
$$

 

find the general solution of the equation.
questions.worked_solution:
The equation

$$
{y}^{′}={y}^{2}-2{e}^{x}y+{e}^{2x}+{e}^{x},
$$

is a Riccati differential equation of the form

$$
{y}^{′}=a(x){y}^{2}+b(x)y+c(x),
$$

where

$$
a(x)=1,\,b(x)=-2{e}^{x},\,c(x)={e}^{2x}+{e}^{x}.
$$

To reduce the given Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation, we use the substitution

$$
y(x)=z(x)+{y}_{0}(x),
$$

where ${y}_{0}(x)$ is a known particular solution.
Differentiating gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={z}^{′}(x)+{y}_{0}^{′}(x).
$$

In our case, ${y}_{0}(x)={e}^{x}.$ Since ${y}_{0}^{′}(x)={e}^{x}$, we have

$$
y=z+{e}^{x}\,⇒\,{y}^{′}={z}^{′}+{e}^{x}.
$$

Let's substitute these expressions into our Riccati equation:

$$
{z}^{′}+{e}^{x}=(z+{e}^{x})^{2}-2{e}^{x}(z+{e}^{x})+{e}^{2x}+{e}^{x}
$$

Now, we expand the right-hand side, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}+{e}^{x} & =({e}^{2x}+2{e}^{x}z+{z}^{2})-(2{e}^{2x}+2{e}^{x}z)+{e}^{2x}+{e}^{x} \\ {z}^{′}+{e}^{x} & ={z}^{2}+{e}^{x} \\ {z}^{′} & ={z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve the obtained equation using separation of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & ={z}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =1 \\ \int \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \int {z}^{-2}\,\text{d}z & =\int \text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{z} & =x+C \\ z & =-\frac{1}{x+C}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

Finally, let's substitute $z=y-{e}^{x}$ to recover the initial variable $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =-\frac{1}{x+C} \\ y-{e}^{x} & =-\frac{1}{x+C} \\ y & =-\frac{1}{x+C}+{e}^{x} \\  & ={e}^{x}-\frac{1}{x+C}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Express this equation in the Bernoulli form

$$

and state the functions $P(x)$ and $Q(x),$ and the value of $n.$

$,\,Q(x)=$
{{field-2}}
$,\,n=$

questions.worked_solution:
A Riccati differential equation has the form

$$
{y}^{′}=a(x){y}^{2}+b(x)y+c(x).
$$

To reduce the given Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation, we use the substitution

$$
y(x)=z(x)+{y}_{0}(x),
$$

where ${y}_{0}(x)$ is a known particular solution.
Differentiating gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={z}^{′}(x)+{y}_{0}^{′}(x).
$$

In our case, ${y}_{0}(x)=-x.$ Since ${y}_{0}^{′}(x)=-1$, we have

$$
y=z-x\,⇒\,{y}^{′}={z}^{′}-1.
$$

Let's substitute these expressions into our Riccati equation:

$$
{z}^{′}-1=-(z-x)^{2}-(2x+1)(-x+z)-(1+x+{x}^{2}).
$$

Now, we expand the right-hand side, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}-1 & =-({x}^{2}+{z}^{2}-2xz)-(-2{x}^{2}+2xz-x+z)-(1+x+{x}^{2}) \\ {z}^{′}-1 & =-{z}^{2}-z-1 \\ {z}^{′}+z & =-{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is a Bernoulli equation of the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x){z}^{n}
$$

where

$$
P(x)=1,\,Q(x)=-1,\,n=2.
$$

questions.problem:
The function ${y}_{0}(x)={x}^{2}$ is a particular solution of the Riccati differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}=x{y}^{2}-2x({x}^{2}+1)y+x({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+2).
$$

Express this equation in the Bernoulli form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x){z}^{n}
$$

and state the functions $P(x)$ and $Q(x),$ and the value of $n.$

$P(x)=$
{{field-1}}
$,\,Q(x)=$
{{field-2}}
$,\,n=$
{{field-3}}
questions.worked_solution:
A Riccati differential equation has the form

$$
{y}^{′}=a(x){y}^{2}+b(x)y+c(x).
$$

To reduce the given Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation, we use the substitution

$$
y(x)=z(x)+{y}_{0}(x),
$$

where ${y}_{0}(x)$ is a known particular solution.
Differentiating gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={z}^{′}(x)+{y}_{0}^{′}(x).
$$

In our case, ${y}_{0}(x)={x}^{2}.$ Since ${y}_{0}^{′}(x)=2x$, we have

$$
y=z+{x}^{2}\,⇒\,{y}^{′}={z}^{′}+2x.
$$

Let's substitute these expressions into our Riccati equation:

$$
{z}^{′}+2x=x(z+{x}^{2})^{2}-2x({x}^{2}+1)(z+{x}^{2})+x({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+2).
$$

Now, we expand the right-hand side, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}+2x & =x(z+{x}^{2})^{2}-2x({x}^{2}+1)(z+{x}^{2})+x({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+2) \\ {z}^{′}+2x & =x{z}^{2}-2xz+2x \\ {z}^{′}+2xz & =x{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is a Bernoulli equation of the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x){z}^{n}
$$

where

$$
P(x)=2x,\,Q(x)=x,\,n=2.
$$

questions.problem:
Given that ${y}_{0}(x)=3x$ is a particular solution of the Riccati differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}=2x\,{y}^{2}-12{x}^{2}y+18{x}^{3}+3
$$

find the general solution of the equation.
questions.worked_solution:
The equation

$$
{y}^{′}=2x\,{y}^{2}-12{x}^{2}y+18{x}^{3}+3,
$$

is a Riccati differential equation of the form

$$
{y}^{′}=a(x){y}^{2}+b(x)y+c(x),
$$

where

$$
a(x)=2x,\,b(x)=-12{x}^{2},\,c(x)=18{x}^{3}+3.
$$

To reduce the given Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation, we use the substitution

$$
y(x)=z(x)+{y}_{0}(x),
$$

where ${y}_{0}(x)$ is a known particular solution.
Differentiating gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={z}^{′}(x)+{y}_{0}^{′}(x).
$$

In our case, ${y}_{0}(x)=3x.$ Since ${y}_{0}^{′}(x)=3$, we have

$$
y=z+3x\,⇒\,{y}^{′}={z}^{′}+3.
$$

Let's substitute these expressions into our Riccati equation:

$$
{z}^{′}+3=2x\,(z+3x)^{2}-12{x}^{2}(z+3x)+18{x}^{3}+3.
$$

Now, we expand the right-hand side, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}+3 & =2x(9{x}^{2}+6xz+{z}^{2})-12{x}^{2}z-36{x}^{3}+18{x}^{3}+3 \\ {z}^{′}+3 & =2x{z}^{2}+3 \\ {z}^{′} & =2x{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve the obtained equation using separation of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =2x{z}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =2x \\ \int \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ \int {z}^{-2}\,\text{d}z & =\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{z} & ={x}^{2}+C \\ z & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+C}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

Finally, let's substitute $z=y-3x$ to recover the initial variable $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+C} \\ y-3x & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+C} \\ y & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+C}+3x \\  & =3x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+C}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that ${y}_{0}(x)=-6x$ is a particular solution of the Riccati differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}=3{y}^{2}+36xy+108{x}^{2}-6
$$

find the general solution of the equation.
questions.worked_solution:
The equation

$$
{y}^{′}=3{y}^{2}+36xy+108{x}^{2}-6,
$$

is a Riccati differential equation of the form

$$
{y}^{′}=a(x){y}^{2}+b(x)y+c(x),
$$

where

$$
a(x)=3,\,b(x)=36x,\,c(x)=108{x}^{2}-6.
$$

To reduce the given Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation, we use the substitution

$$
y(x)=z(x)+{y}_{0}(x),
$$

where ${y}_{0}(x)$ is a known particular solution.
Differentiating gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={z}^{′}(x)+{y}_{0}^{′}(x).
$$

In our case, ${y}_{0}(x)=-6x.$ Since ${y}_{0}^{′}(x)=-6$, we have

$$
y=z-6x\,⇒\,{y}^{′}={z}^{′}-6.
$$

Let's substitute these expressions into our Riccati equation:

$$
{z}^{′}-6=3(z-6x)^{2}+36x(z-6x)+108{x}^{2}-6.
$$

Now, we expand the right-hand side, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}-6 & =3(36{x}^{2}-12xz+{z}^{2})+36xz-216{x}^{2}+108{x}^{2}-6 \\ {z}^{′}-6 & =3{z}^{2}-6 \\ {z}^{′} & =3{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve the obtained equation using separation of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =3{z}^{2} \\ \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =3 \\ \int \frac{1}{{z}^{2}}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int 3\,\text{d}x \\ \int {z}^{-2}\,\text{d}z & =\int 3\,\text{d}x \\ -\frac{1}{z} & =3x+C \\ z & =-\frac{1}{3x+C}\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

Finally, let's substitute $z=y+6x$ (that is, $y=z-6x$) to recover the initial variable $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =-\frac{1}{3x+C} \\ y+6x & =-\frac{1}{3x+C} \\ y & =-\frac{1}{3x+C}-6x \\  & =-6x-\frac{1}{3x+C}\end{aligned}
$$
